Agility (Japanese: こうそくいどう High-speed Movement) is a non-damaging Psychic-type move introduced in Generation I. It is TR12 in Generation VIII.

Effect

Agility increases the user's Speed by two stages.

Agility can be used as part of a Pokémon Contest combination, with the user gaining extra three appeal points if the move Double Team was used in the prior turn. It is also part of a Contest Spectacular combination and using it will cause Baton Pass and Electro Ball to give extra three appeal points if used in the next turn.

If powered up by a Psychium Z into Z-Agility, all of the user's lowered stats are reset.

In other games

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon series

In Red Rescue Team and Blue Rescue Team, Agility is a move with 22PP that ignores accuracy and evasion checks. It targets all team members in the same room, increasing their Movement Speed by one level. In hallways, this move targets Pokémon up two tiles away (or one in one-tile darkness). This move is affected by Snatch and Taunt.

In Explorers of Time, Darkness and Sky, this move's PP has been decreased to 12.

Super Smash Bros. series

In Super Smash Bros. Melee and Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, Agility is Pichu's up special. It is similar to Pikachu's Quick Attack in that it is a fast dash that can be done in two different directions, but unlike Quick Attack, it does not deal damage to the opponent, rather, it damages Pichu. Pichu cannot legitimately learn Agility in the main games.

  • In the English dubs of The Ancient Puzzle of Pokémopolis and Hot Matches!, Brock commanded his Vulpix to use Agility, which it could not legitimately learn until Generation VIII. In the original Japanese versions, Brock instead commanded Vulpix to use Quick Attack.
  • In the English dub of Power Play!, Gary told his Umbreon to use Agility, which it is incapable of learning legitimately. In the original Japanese version, Umbreon was just told to use its footwork to dodge an attack.
